audit.title: Cross-Chain Token Standard - Overview

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Working — opens with a clean canonical statement: "The Cross-Chain Token (CCT) standard offers a streamlined and decentralized approach to enabling token transfers across blockchains…" and each Key Concept leads with its definition. Weak — the opening paragraph is a ~180-word block that buries specifics.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Working — 27 headings, 1 H1, no level skips, no section over 600 words (max 435), sensible chunk boundaries. Weak — 0 tables; the four handling mechanisms and rate-limit parameters are prime table candidates, and the "Token-Specific Transfer Mechanisms" bullets are long, dense list items.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Working — "$16 trillion in Total Value Enabled," version-gated feature ("Starting from v1.5.1… zero-downtime upgrades"), concrete "10 LINK" transfer walkthroughs. Weak — measured facts flag 0 numerals with units and vague quantifiers ("several," "most," "significant").

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Working — links to chainlist.org, a GitHub primary-source contract, CCIP Directory. Weak — one opaque "here" link (measured); no links to the CCIP whitepaper/spec or canonical rate-limit definitions.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Strong — the Key Concepts section (Token Developer, Token Administrator, EOA, Smart Account, Token Pool) is textbook verbatim-liftable. Minor: a stray double period ("TokenAdminRegistry..").

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak — 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no `datePublished`/`dateModified`, 0 og/twitter tags in the served head. The visible "Last Updated" date is body text only, invisible to parsers.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Weak but context-adjusted — a concept page legitimately carries little code, but the ETH-transfer procedure references `EthSenderContract.sol` with no inline snippet or config; a short liftable example would help agents.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Working — covers "what is CCT," motivations, mechanisms, native-gas-token transfer steps. Weak — concept-titled headings only; no FAQ/troubleshooting and no symptom- or question-phrased headings ("How do I transfer ETH cross-chain?", "Which token handling mechanism should I use?").

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong — unambiguous, consistent naming of CCT/CCIP/token pool entities. Minor redundancy across the benefits subsections.

audit.summary: This is a well-written conceptual overview of Chainlink's Cross-Chain Token (CCT) standard, strongest in its crisp Key Concepts glossary and consistent terminology — both highly liftable. Its biggest structural weakness is the absence of a comparison table for the four token-handling mechanisms (Burn/Mint, Lock/Mint, Burn/Unlock, Lock/Unlock), which are described in prose an engine must reassemble rather than extract. The single largest GEO liability is machine-readability: no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, and no `dateModified` in the served `<head>` (the "Last Updated: 2025-05-19" line lives only in body text). Honest verdict: solid, retrievable content held back by missing metadata and the lack of scannable comparison structures.

recommendations.title: Add a comparison table for the four token-handling mechanisms
recommendations.issue: four mechanisms described only in separate prose blocks; 0 tables on page.
recommendations.change: add a table with columns `Mechanism | Source-chain action | Destination-chain action | When to use | Example token`, one row each for Burn/Mint, Lock/Mint, Burn/Unlock, Lock/Unlock (rows populated from existing text — LINK, WETH, USDC).
recommendations.why: tables let engines extract the *reason* for choosing a mechanism and answer "which mechanism for X" queries in one liftable unit.

recommendations.title: Add question/symptom-phrased headings and a short FAQ
recommendations.where: the native-gas section and end of page.
recommendations.issue: heading "Token Handling Mechanisms" and note "Transferring Native Gas Tokens" don't match how devs query.
recommendations.change: retitle to "How do I transfer native ETH cross-chain with CCIP?" and add an H2 FAQ ("Which token handling mechanism should I use?", "Do CCTs require liquidity pools?", "What are token pool rate limits?").
recommendations.why: question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses even when the answer is present verbatim.

recommendations.title: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with canonical and `dateModified`
recommendations.issue: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no dates in served head.
recommendations.change: add JSON-LD `TechArticle` with `headline`, `dateModified: 2025-05-19`, canonical URL, and `inLanguage`; surface the existing "Last Updated" as a machine-readable date.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and visible freshness raise parse-trust and E-E-A-T; note this is likely a site-level fix.

recommendations.title: Add a rate-limits parameter table with units
recommendations.issue: "maximum capacity and a refill rate" described qualitatively; 0 numerals carry units.
recommendations.change: define TPRL parameters in a small table (`Parameter | Meaning | Unit`, e.g. capacity in tokens, refill rate in tokens/second) and link the CCIP Directory as the live-values source.
recommendations.why: quantitative claims with units are among the highest-lift changes for citation.

recommendations.title: Replace the opaque "here" link and add a spec/primary-source citation
recommendations.where: Token Manager NOTE ("Read more about it [here]") and Motivations.
recommendations.issue: "[here]" gives engines no anchor context; measured 1 opaque link.
recommendations.change: relabel to "Read more about the CCIP Token Manager"; add an inline link to the CCT/CCIP whitepaper or spec near the first CCT definition.
recommendations.why: descriptive anchor text and primary-source links raise citation rate and disambiguate entities.

recommendations.title: Tighten vague quantifiers and lead the intro with specifics
recommendations.change: front-load a one-sentence definition + one concrete number (e.g. supported-chain count or TVE) as the first liftable line; replace vague quantifiers with figures where known.
recommendations.why: self-contained, specific opening sentences are preferentially lifted; vague qualifiers underperform.

antiPatterns: Freshness signal present in body ("Last Updated: 2025-05-19") but invisible to parsers (no `dateModified`).
No walls-of-prose violation at section level, but the intro paragraph and the LINK bullet are dense single blocks.
offPageNotes: JSON-LD, canonical URL, and og/head metadata are almost certainly template/site-level fixes rather than page-authored — coordinate with the docs platform; CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a fuller read.
`llms.txt` is already referenced at the top of the page — good site-level discoverability signal.
Image alt text could not be assessed ("(Image: Image)" placeholders suggest missing descriptive alt/captions that would otherwise aid extraction of the mechanism diagrams).
